header.title: Open Speech Studio
header.heroAlt: Open Speech Studio: the speech models from tiny to large-v3-turbo, with speed, accuracy and memory use per model
header.label: Speech recognition
header.tagline: Talk instead of type, in any app and without the cloud
header.desc: Hold a hotkey, speak and let go: your text appears where your cursor was. Transcribe meetings and recordings too. Recognition runs on your own computer, free and without a subscription.

meta.description: Free, open-source speech recognition on your own computer: dictate into any app with a hotkey, transcribe meetings and audio or video files, and have text read aloud. Whisper, 99 languages. For Windows, macOS and Linux.
meta.title: Open Speech Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

dictate.alt: Start screen saying the app is ready, with the hotkey to start dictating
dictate.title: Speak your text into any app
dictate.desc: Hold Ctrl+Win, say your sentence and let go: the text appears where your cursor is, in your email, report, chat or code editor. Prefer to press once to start and once to stop? That works too, and you choose the hotkey.

meeting.alt: Record and transcribe screen with language, interval, record button and the microphone meter
meeting.title: Minutes of your meeting, without the cloud
meeting.desc: Record a site meeting or conversation; the app transcribes along in segments of a few minutes. In an online meeting it also records your PC audio, so participants in Teams, Zoom or Meet end up in the transcript (Windows). Export to .txt, Markdown or .odt.

files.alt: Transcribe files screen with a drop zone for audio and video files
files.title: Transcribe recordings and videos
files.desc: Drop audio or video files into the app, from WAV and MP3 to MP4 and MOV. Several files are processed at once. Copy the text, save it as .txt or have every transcript saved to a folder automatically.

tts.alt: Text to speech screen with voice selection, sliders for speed and pauses, and the voice library
tts.title: Have text read aloud in a natural voice
tts.desc: Pick a Dutch, Flemish or English voice, set speed, expressiveness and pauses, and have a text read aloud. A voice is about 60 MB and runs on your own processor. Read aloud works on Windows for now.

gpu.alt: Speech settings with language, an active NVIDIA graphics card, auto paste and sound effects
gpu.title: Quick on an ordinary laptop, faster with a graphics card
gpu.desc: Choose a model that suits your computer: the small models run smoothly on the processor, the large ones are more accurate. On Windows an NVIDIA graphics card is used automatically, and you see which card is active and how much memory it has.

features.label: Features
features.heading: Dictate, record meetings and transcribe in one app
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

hotkey.title: Hotkey in any app
hotkey.desc: Ctrl+Win or Ctrl+Shift+Space, or your own combination of two or three keys.

mode.title: Hold or toggle
mode.desc: Hold the key while you speak, or press once to start and again to stop.

paste.title: Text at your cursor
paste.desc: The text is typed where your cursor is. One checkbox adds an Enter, handy for chat and AI prompts.

sounds.title: Sound at start and stop
sounds.desc: Hear when recording starts and finishes, with two sound sets and your own volume.

mictest.title: Microphone test
mictest.desc: Pick your microphone, see the level and check with a test sentence that recognition works.

online.title: Online meetings
online.desc: Microphone and PC audio together, so participants in Teams, Zoom or Meet end up in the transcript. On Windows.

segments.title: Transcribes in segments
segments.desc: Automatically every few minutes, or in between with Save segment, without stopping the recording.

meters.title: Microphone and PC levels
meters.desc: See during the recording whether audio is coming in, with peak, average and clipping.

meetexport.title: Minutes as .txt, .md or .odt
meetexport.desc: Copy everything or export; the file opens straight in your editor. Saving automatically to a fixed folder works too.

formats.title: Audio and video
formats.desc: WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, M4A, MP4, MKV, AVI, MOV and more. Drop them into the app or browse.

parallel.title: Several files at once
parallel.desc: Files are processed side by side; you choose how many at a time.

txt.title: Save as text
txt.desc: Copy the text, export as .txt or have every transcript saved to a folder automatically.

models.title: Eight speech models
models.desc: From tiny (75 MB) to large-v3 (3.1 GB). For each model you see speed, accuracy and memory use.

languages.title: 99 languages
languages.desc: Choose a fixed language or let the app detect the spoken language.

dictionary.title: Your own dictionary
dictionary.desc: Teach the app names, abbreviations and jargon, with a replacement if you like.

gpu.title: Graphics card or processor
gpu.desc: On Windows an NVIDIA graphics card helps out; without one, everything runs on the processor.

local.title: Everything on your own PC
local.desc: Your voice and your text never leave your computer. No account, no subscription, no limit.

tts.title: Read aloud
tts.desc: Nine voices in Dutch, Flemish and English, with speed, expressiveness and pauses. On Windows.

ui.title: App in 25 languages
ui.desc: From Dutch and English to Turkish, Polish and Japanese.

tray.title: Always at hand
tray.desc: The app waits in the system tray and is ready as soon as you press the hotkey.

download.title: Download v0.12.2
download.lead: Free, no account needed. For Windows, macOS and Linux.
download.label: Download
download.mobileNote: Open Speech Studio is a desktop app. Download it on your computer.

online.title: Online meetings
online.desc: Record microphone and PC audio together, so everyone in Teams, Zoom or Meet ends up in the transcript (Windows).

macos.title: Back on macOS
macos.desc: For Apple Silicon and Intel, with Ctrl+Shift+Space to dictate. Read aloud and PC audio will follow later.

linux.title: Linux ready to go
linux.desc: AppImage, .deb and .rpm with the speech engine and a model included. Ctrl+Win now works on Linux too (X11).

models.title: Two new models
models.desc: Compact versions of large-v3-turbo (574 and 874 MB): more accurate than small, smaller than medium.

export.title: Minutes open right away
export.desc: Saved meeting minutes in .txt, .md or .odt open straight in your editor.

signed.title: Signed downloads
signed.desc: The Windows installers are signed; the Linux packages come with a signature (.asc) you can verify.

whatsnew.label: New in v0.12
whatsnew.title: Online meetings, now on macOS and Linux too
whatsnew.desc: Version 0.12 also records PC audio in online meetings, brings installers for macOS and Linux and adds two mid-size speech models.

files.a: Audio and video: WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, M4A, MP4, MKV, AVI, MOV and more. Dictation and meetings go straight through your microphone.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: Yes. Open Speech Studio is a desktop app; there is no web version. After installing, you download a speech model of your choice in the app. The macOS and Linux packages already include one.

price.q: What does Open Speech Studio cost?
price.a: Nothing. The app is free and open source under the Apache-2.0 licence, with no account, subscription or limit on minutes.

save.q: In which file format is my work saved?
save.a: Dictated text goes straight into the app where your cursor is. File transcripts are saved as .txt, meeting minutes as .txt, Markdown or .odt. Both can also be saved automatically to a folder you choose.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Linux (AppImage, .deb and .rpm). On macOS the app is not yet signed with an Apple Developer ID: open it the first time with right-click and Open. Read aloud and recording PC audio do not work there yet. The .dmg for Intel is on the GitHub releases page.

privacy.q: Does my voice go to the internet?
privacy.a: No. Recognition runs with Whisper on your own computer. You only need internet to download models and voices.

hardware.q: Do I need a powerful computer?
hardware.a: No. The small models run smoothly on an ordinary processor with 1 to 2 GB of memory. For the largest models, an NVIDIA graphics card with at least 6 GB of video memory is recommended.

languages.a: 99 languages, including Dutch, English, French, German, Turkish and Spanish. Choose a fixed language or let the app detect it. The app itself is available in 25 languages.

jargon.q: Does it recognise jargon and names?
jargon.a: Add names, abbreviations and jargon to the dictionary, with a replacement if you like. From the small model upwards, jargon and accents are recognised noticeably better.

tauri.title: Tauri 2
tauri.desc: A thin native shell in Rust for Windows, macOS and Linux.

whisper.title: whisper.cpp
whisper.desc: OpenAI's Whisper models, run locally, with CUDA on Windows and Metal on Apple Silicon.

solid.title: SolidJS and Vite
solid.desc: A fast TypeScript interface, with 25 languages and the OpenAEC house style.

cpal.title: cpal
cpal.desc: Audio from the microphone and, on Windows, PC audio through WASAPI loopback.

piper.title: Piper
piper.desc: Local text-to-speech with Dutch, Flemish and English voices.

release.title: GitHub Actions
release.desc: Every release is built and checked automatically per platform; the Windows and Linux packages are signed.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: For those who want to know how it is built.
